title: Staging lane selector and performance dossier for deployment pinning
creator: Diego Alvarez
description:
Problem: Customers onboarding models often need to pin a specific model binary or variant to particular deployment lanes (staging, canary, production) while simultaneously understanding the latency/cost/quality trade-offs. Current console flows scatter pin controls across the model detail page and the rollout page, and performance profiles are buried in a separate tab. That creates friction for engineers doing fast iterations and increases risk during rollouts.

Proposal: Add a unified 'Staging Lane Selector' component on the model release workflow that: 1) shows available model versions and variants for a given model, 2) allows pinning a version to a named lane (staging/canary/prod) with a single confirmation, 3) surfaces a compact performance dossier for each version (median p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, quality score delta against baseline, known caveats like quantization/kv-cache behavior), and 4) exposes a one-click 'Publish profile' action to attach a performance profile to a pinned version for downstream routing and autoscaling recommendations.

Design goals: reduce cognitive load during pinning, make performance trade-offs visible inline, preserve ability to do canary/weighted rollouts, provide audit metadata for compliance.

Key UX elements: Staging Lane Selector (card list of lanes), Version Tile (version id, build tag, annotation, small perf sparkline), Performance Dossier (expandable panel with metrics + quick compare against currently live version), Pin Confirmation (intent modal with impact summary, estimated cost delta, affected routes), Publish Profile Flow (wizard to validate perf profile and attach to version), Rollback affordance (link to previous pinned version + reason).

Acceptance criteria: 1) PMs and Engs can pin a version to a staging lane in <= 3 clicks, 2) Performance dossier loads under 500ms for typical model catalogs, 3) Publish profile action stores a profile and surfaces it in per-route dashboards, 4) Audit log entry created for every pin/publish action, 5) E2E integration tests cover pin, publish, canary rollout, and rollback.
activities: 2025-01-21 - Kickoff with design and runtime leads; agreed on single-pane flow for pick/pin/publish
2025-01-28 - Design review: provided wireframes for staging lane cards and version tiles; DES feedback: make cost delta more prominent
2025-02-03 - Eng feasibility sync: ENG proposes caching perf dossier results and lazy-loading full metrics to meet 500ms target
2025-02-06 - PM notes updated acceptance criteria to include audit logging and E2E tests
2025-02-10 - Prototyping: interactive prototype linked below; initial usability test with 5 engineers highlighted confusion around 'Publish profile' semantics
2025-02-12 - Decision: rename 'Publish profile' to 'Attach performance snapshot' to reduce false expectation of auto-deploy; next action: update copy and run microcopy A/B with 10 users
